A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Control-GIC and retain the same central framework. All 15 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Kodak and DIV2K compression results, decoder ablations, entropy-coding comparisons, and fine-grained bitrate-control experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original compression experiments on Kodak, DIV2K, and CLIC2020, alongside efficiency measurements, ablations, and extremely-low-bitrate results.

M1.justification: The granularity-based encoder, vector quantization, conditional decoder feature replacement, statistical Huffman coding, and training objectives remain substantively unchanged. The lookup-table and discriminator descriptions add documentation without establishing a changed compression procedure. Codebook capacity changes are experimental settings.

E1.justification: v3 adds CLIC2020 evaluation using 428 high-resolution images. OpenImages training and Kodak/DIV2K evaluation remain within the same natural-image compression task. DIV2K was already evaluated in v1 Appendix A.1; its appearance in the later main text is a relocation.

E2.justification: v3 adds MRIC and MS-ILLM to the main comparisons. The DIV2K comparison also gains VVC, M&S, SCR, and CDC beyond v1's labeled BPG, CTC, and HiFiC comparators. Appendix A.6 newly compares against Mao et al., explicitly using approximated published results rather than rerunning that baseline.

E3.justification: The reported codebook size changes from 16,384 to 1,024 vectors, and training increases from 165k to 600k iterations. KID replaces IS in the evaluation framework, while the main Kodak comparison drops its FID/IS panels. New protocols include common-GPU timing, VVC-anchored LPIPS BD-rate comparisons, and fully coarse-grained compression below 0.05 bpp. These reported revisions do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds an efficiency analysis relating encoding/decoding time and training cost to BD-rate saving, plus granularity-sensitivity and small-face failure studies. Fine-control evidence changes from the earlier scatter plot and numerical table to new visual demonstrations. The decoder-component ablation remains, and the existing entropy-coding comparison moves into Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The earlier per-image bitrate scatter concerns rate-control behavior rather than uncertainty across experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 revises benchmark and decoder-ablation curves and adds efficiency, CLIC2020, and extremely-low-bitrate results. Table 3 reports Control-GIC at 0.0381 bpp with LPIPS 0.115 on Kodak and 0.0372 bpp with LPIPS 0.086 on CLIC2020. Earlier Kodak FID/IS panels and v1 Table 2's empirical rows disappear; entropy-coding Table 1 retains its values. Changed training settings prevent interpreting revised curves as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds Equation 12, deriving theoretical index and mask bitrates from granularity ratios and average code length. Its mask-rate equality contains a factor-of-four algebraic inconsistency. The existing spatial-entropy equations move unchanged to Appendix A.2; this relocation does not introduce a new proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of unified, fine-grained bitrate adaptation and the same three technical contributions remain. v3 drops the explicit abstract/contribution claim about single-pass compression of an entire dataset under constrained bitrates and shifts the introduction's comparative emphasis toward flexibility and compression efficiency.

C2.justification: The applicability discussion changes substantially: v1's explicit limitation above 1.0 bpp disappears, while v3 discusses small-face reconstruction failures and discrepancies between predicted and actual bitrate. v3 also acknowledges MSE-based methods' PSNR advantage, interprets the new efficiency comparisons, and adds a stronger nearly-lossless reconstruction interpretation of decoder feature preservation.

D1.justification: v3 documents the bitrate lookup construction, average code length of 10.3875, patch-based discriminator, and efficiency-measurement setup. It also identifies DIV2K as the decoder-ablation dataset. Conversely, v1's explicit four-GPU count and BPG color-format/bit-depth settings are omitted. These are documentation changes beyond the reported configuration revisions.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to MRIC, MS-ILLM, recent VQ-based compression work by Xue and Jia, Huffman coding, and the patch-based discriminator. Some earlier references, including Hoogeboom, Rippel, and the IS reference, disappear. The overall positioning around neural compression, rate adaptation, and VQGAN remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, method explanations, and experimental narrative undergo substantial rewriting. Spatial-entropy details move to the appendix, while DIV2K and entropy-coding comparisons move into the main text. The appendices are reorganized into seven subsections, and the author block and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the opening motivation figure, adds an entropy-allocation inset to the architecture diagram, and removes the separate entropy illustration. Benchmark panels and qualitative comparisons are redesigned, and new efficiency plots, granularity examples, low-bitrate comparisons, and tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Stronger comparators and the common-hardware efficiency analysis make the claimed quality-versus-efficiency trade-off more assessable. CLIC2020 evaluation and small-face examples add useful validation and expose a failure condition. These gains are tempered by removal of the earlier high-bitrate limitation and new inconsistencies in Equation 12 and Figure 7's granularity labels, leaving a limited net improvement.
